title: Patchers
finding: Root changes on the device itself
findingApplied_one: Root changes on the device itself · {{applied}} of {{count}} patch applied
findingApplied_other: Root changes on the device itself · {{applied}} of {{count}} patches applied
noDevices: No devices connected. Connect a device first, then come back to patch it.
statusFailed: Patch status could not be read. {{error}}
unsupported: Patchers are only available for the Linux models (T5, T6, T7, D4H, D4SH, W7H). This device uses a different platform.
reachesAt: The server reaches this device at <ip>{{ip}}</ip>.
ipUnknown: Device IP unknown: wait for a state report before patching.
pick: Pick a patch to read what it changes and how to undo it, then apply or remove it.
risk: Each patch runs shell commands on the device as root, at your own risk: it can brick the device and leaves it outside its warranty. Patches live only on the writable /system partition; the read-only /app partition is never modified.

blocker.greyed: The device already holds an MQTT session, which proves this patch is in place.
blocker.noIp: Device IP unknown. Wait for the device to send a state report before patching.

action.undoApply: Remove undoes it: the files are deleted from /system and the device reboots without the patch.
action.undoRemove: The device reboots without this patch. Other patches stay active; with none left it boots stock firmware.
action.spaceBody: Needs about {{size}} free. Free space is checked on the device before anything is written; the exact need is measured then and is usually smaller.
action.sshKeyHint: Root SSH on port 22 accepts this key only: ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-sha2.
action.accepted: Accepted. Progress comes from the server over the live connection; a run takes minutes.
action.stepUp: Asks for your password, then shows progress here step by step.
